_source: Generated by backend/scripts/calibrate_donor_gates.py from the cached FEC Schedule A receipts and employer/occupation totals of a production snapshot: labels from the FEC's own fields (conduit and memo codes, entity types, receipt types, the employer and occupation fields), never by hand (the script's docstring gives each). Each threshold: the grid point whose precision's exact lower 95% bound is highest on half the labels (split by a hash of the text), used only when that bound is at least 0.8, else null (the embedding tier never fires); held_out scores the other half.

employer_skip.not_applied_because: The labels miss a class: status values (SELF-EMPLOYED, NONE, INFORMATION REQUESTED) are a filing convention neither field testifies to, so 'never written as an occupation' counts them as organizations, and the itemized-receipt paths have no two-field test to fall back on.

transfer_memo.not_applied_because: The fit trades recall (29.5% to 8.7%) for precision (76% to 92%): a missed transfer counts money moved between committees as a donation, a false one drops a real donation, and which costs a page more is a decision, not a measurement.

donor_type.not_applied_because: Closing the tier hands its names to the kNN tier and normalize_finance's Org/Employees fallback, whose accuracy on these names is unmeasured (the learning store the kNN reads is cleared with every fingerprint change); 90% of the names it meets are PACs, so the fallback may be worse.

skip_type.not_applied_because: A closed skip keeps individuals' names (7.7% of the names the tier meets) as donors under a fallback type; whether that is better than a 61%-precise skip is a judgement on which error a page should show.
